title: Role mapping validation, dual-write divergence detection, and customer cutover runbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Safely migrate customers from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with minimal disruption. Deliverables: (1) deterministic role-mapping validator that flags incompatible mappings; (2) dual-write runtime with divergence detectors and automated read-repair candidates; (3) a step-by-step customer cutover and rollback runbook including customer-facing comms and escalation playbook; (4) audit logging for every mapping change and migration step to satisfy compliance requests.
acceptance_criteria: Role-mapping validator runs against 100% of active orgs and reports >95% of incompatible mappings as actionable items
Dual-write enabled in shadow mode for all clusters and divergence rate measured <0.1% before opt-in cutovers
Reconciliation job created that surfaces per-org mismatch metrics and auto-generates repair PRs for simple cases
Cutover runbook validated in staging (dry-run) and SSO/SAML mappings preserved for test tenants
Audit logs capture old_role -> new_role mapping, actor, timestamp, and migration step for every change
notes_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting with Security, Platform, and DX. Agreed validator must be reversible and non-destructive.

2025-03-03: First divergence detector run produced 74 mismatches (0.18% of sampled writes). Root causes: race conditions in team rename, legacy wildcard role.
2025-03-06: Reconciliation job design approved. Will prioritize simple 1:1 mappings for automated repair and create tickets for complex cases.

rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Shadow verification: dual-write enabled with writes mirrored to rbac_v2 but responses read from v1. Divergence detectors run hourly.
Phase 1 - Canary cutovers: pick 10 low-impact orgs (consent obtained) and perform full cutover during maintenance window. Validate SSO sign-in paths and admin permissions.
Phase 2 - Batched migration: group orgs by complexity (1:1 mapping, multi-group, custom roles). Run automated backfill for 1:1 group, manual for custom roles.
Phase 3 - Full cutover: schedule per-region maintenance windows, enable v2 as primary with v1 as read-only fallback for 72 hours.
Phase 4 - Post-cutover reconciliation: run reconciliation job at T+1h, T+6h, T+24h and escalate any org with >0.05% divergence to SE on-call.
Rollback plan: flip flag to route writes back to v1 (fast-path). Run targeted read-repair jobs to reconcile partial changes made in v2 during rollback.
Opt-out: provide an org-level feature flag for customers requiring more time; for regulated customers we will schedule dedicated migration windows.
backfill_strategy: Backfill worker runs in k8s cron job with controlled concurrency and per-org rate limits.
Idempotent operations: each backfill writes include migration_id and idempotency_key so re-runs are safe.
Staging-first: backfill is exercised against staging orgs and a 5% production sample before broad rollout.
Partial backfill detection: workers emit metrics for records processed, conflicts found, and repairs applied. Alert threshold at 0.2% conflicts.
Edge-case handling: for custom role compositions that cannot be represented in RBAC v2, create 'legacy-role-compat' shim and tag those orgs for manual review.
dual_write_strategy: All writes go to both v1 and v2 when feature flag enabled. Writes include: actor_id, client_request_id, timestamp, and migration_id.
Idempotency: use composite key (actor_id + client_request_id + migration_id) to avoid duplicate writes under retries.
Divergence detectors: hourly job compares hashes of role mappings per-org between stores. If mismatch, record first_seen, last_seen, and sample diff into talent-recon index.
Read-repair candidates: if mismatch is trivially resolvable (exact 1:1 mapping), auto-apply repair to the older store with proper audit log entry.
Shadow read verification: sample 1% of reads to verify v2 produces same authorization decision as v1. Log discrepancies for root cause triage.
Feature-flagging & throttling: dual-write ramp constrained by global ops quota to avoid overwhelming v2 clusters.
Monitoring: add metrics rbac.dualwrite.success, rbac.dualwrite.divergence_rate, rbac.recovery.auto_applied_count.
cutover_checklist: Pre-cutover: All failing validator checks resolved or mitigated; stakeholder sign-off obtained (PM, Security, SRE).
Pre-cutover: Audit log KMS keys rotated and migration_id added to KMS envelope.
During cutover: Enable dual-write -> routing flag to prefer v2 for reads for canary orgs. Monitor greenlights on auth smoke tests for 15 minutes.
During cutover: Run SSO login smoke tests for each IdP type used by the org (SAML, OIDC).
Immediate rollback window: 60 minutes for canary, 6 hours for batch. Have rollback playbook and the CLI command to flip routing flags ready.
Post-cutover: Execute reconciliation pass and file per-org migration summary to customer dashboard and audit trail.
Post-cutover: Notify customer success team and create follow-up CS tickets for any minor permission regressions.
customer_communication: Pre-cutover email template: (subject) Upcoming RBAC migration window — what to expect. Body includes maintenance window, expected impact (brief), opt-out link, and support contact.
Canary confirmation: For selected canary orgs we will request explicit consent and provide a test checklist for SSO admins.
Post-cutover summary: Link to per-org migration log, list of automatic repairs applied, manual changes required, and instructions for admins to re-grant any uncommon permissions.
Status page snippet for major cutovers: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rbac-migration-2025
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Divergence writes lead to inconsistent permission checks. Mitigation: block production promotion if divergence_rate > 0.2% across sampled orgs.
Risk: SSO mapping breaks for complex SAML attribute transforms. Mitigation: detect transforms during validator run and schedule manual mapping sessions with customer.
Risk: Audit trail incomplete for rollbacks. Mitigation: every migration change is logged with migration_id and stored in immutable audit index with 1 year retention and KMS encryption.
Risk: Performance regression on v2 under dual-write. Mitigation: throttle dual-write and fallback to v1 on SLA breach, alert SRE.
Risk: Customer confusion after role structure change. Mitigation: include a clear before/after role map in customer communication and provide support walk-throughs.
test_plan: Unit: validator test-suite covering edge cases (inheritance, wildcard roles, group flattening).
Integration: dual-write system test that simulates retries, reorders, and partial failures; assert idempotency and divergence detection.
Staging dry-run: full migration rehearsal against staging orgs including SSO sign-ins and admin flows.
Canary smoke tests: auth decision checks, audit-log presence, and integration tests with console role displays.
Chaos test: simulate v2 delayed writes and ensure read-path follows fallback policies without leaking inconsistent grants.
audit_log_plan: Every mapped change writes audit event with fields: migration_id, org_id, actor_id, old_role, new_role, reason, source (validator|backfill|manual).
Audit events indexed into immutable index with HMAC verification to detect tampering.
Retention & export: 1 year retention in hot index, 3 year cold archive for enterprise customers with export tool for compliance requests.
On rollback: produce a signed rollback manifest summarizing changes reverted and the rationale for each revert.
sso_mapping_notes: Validator extracts SAML attribute transforms and canonicalizes to a mapping table for RBAC v2 import.
If a mapping requires custom transformation not representable in v2, annotate the org and surface to PM and Solutions Engineering to craft a manual mapping.
During canary we will run IdP-initiated and SP-initiated SSO flows to ensure both mapping paths are intact.
Record sample SAML Requests/Responses (with PII redaction) to debugging index for post-mortem if auth regressions occur.
